title: From a prompt to a playable runner: this is where I got stuck
author: GeorgeTsang16
selftext:
I’m sharing a short clip from a small browser runner I have been working on.

The original idea was simple: a tiny character running through a foggy city, trying to survive, collect energy, and keep moving forward while larger threats begin to fill the road.

I do not have a coding background, so I started by using Soonlab to generate a basic playable demo. That first version was rough, but it gave me something important: an actual game loop I could see and react to instead of an idea that only existed in my head.

After that, I downloaded the HTML and brought it into Codex. I have been using it to inspect the code, adjust movement and collision behavior, revise the UI, and slowly understand what each part of the game is doing. I also used AI-generated placeholder assets for the city, characters, pickups, and effects so the game could have a visual identity early on.

The current version is playable, but I am not satisfied with it yet.

The foggy city has some of the mood I wanted, but I think the player is too easy to lose in the scene. The road, obstacles, pickups, camera, and character movement do not always feel like they belong to the same rhythm. Sometimes the game looks busy without feeling exciting. Sometimes I add an effect or a new object, hoping it will make the game feel better, but it only makes the screen harder to read.

This has been the most useful part of the process for me so far: AI helped me get past the blank page, but it did not tell me what the game should feel like. It can generate another building, another effect, or another mechanic. It cannot reliably tell me which one is actually making the experience worse.

I am trying to resist adding more content until the basic loop feels clearer.

**If you watch the clip, I would really value feedback on three things:**

1. What do you think the player is supposed to focus on first?
2. What feels weakest right now: the camera, player readability, obstacle design, feedback, pacing, or UI?
3. If you could change only one thing before adding more features, what would it be?

I’m still very early in learning game creation, so detailed criticism is genuinely useful. I would rather understand what is not working than keep asking AI to decorate the problem.

And if you want to try this game, here is the link: [Climate Chase](https://www.soonlab.ai/game/4106)  
I've uploaded this version back to the platform, but it's still not perfect. You can try it out though.
